editorial:
Ever wonder what happens when you reconnect with an old best friend who has completely lost their way? You get to see that play out here with two guys who grew up together but ended up in totally different worlds. One guy has the perfect life with a nice marriage and a steady job, while the other is a total mess who is unemployed and drifting through life. What starts as a simple plan to grab a drink quickly turns into a wild ride. It feels like a slow slide into chaos as their old bond brings out a reckless, aggressive side of their personalities that they can't seem to stop.

The acting is the best part because you really feel the tension between these two opposites. While the story can feel a bit heavy at times, the way it shows their friendship is very real. You will probably find yourself shouting at the screen as they make bad choices, but that is what makes it gripping. If you want to see it, I suggest renting it on Apple TV for a quick watch or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection if you like owning high-quality copies of indie dramas.
endingExplained: By the end, the two men have pushed each other too far, leading to a violent clash that ruins everything they tried to protect. They lose their money and their peace of mind in a series of bad decisions. However, as the dust settles, they realize that despite the wreckage they caused, they are the only people who truly understand each other. They end up alone together, clinging to a broken friendship because it is all they have left.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies about toxic friendships.
